name: Enfortumab vedotin (single agent)

biomarkers.note: Enfortumab vedotin is a Nectin-4-directed antibody-drug conjugate delivering the microtubule inhibitor MMAE. Nectin-4 is broadly expressed in urothelial carcinoma and no companion biomarker test is required to treat. Applies to bladder (#57) and upper-tract (#58) urothelial carcinoma. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G).

lineOfTherapy: subsequent-line for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after prior platinum-based chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: prior platinum-based chemotherapy and prior PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, BL-G (Enfortumab vedotin after PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and platinum-containing chemotherapy; references 24, 30, 31)

drugs.name: Enfortumab vedotin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: DeVita 12e line 20821-20827 (enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg weekly x3 of a 4-week cycle, urothelial)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 20821-20827: 1.25 mg/kg IV on days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle (cap at 100 kg body weight). Enfortumab vedotin specific safety (hyperglycemia/DKA, peripheral neuropathy, severe skin reactions including SJS/TEN, ocular toxicity) applies.

supportiveCare: HYPERGLYCEMIA: monitor blood glucose before each dose; hold for hyperglycemia (serious/fatal diabetic ketoacidosis reported, including in patients without pre-existing diabetes).
PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY: assess before each dose; sensory and motor neuropathy can be dose-limiting - hold/reduce/discontinue per severity.
SKIN REACTIONS: monitor for severe cutaneous reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN); discontinue for severe skin reactions.
OCULAR toxicity (dry eye/keratopathy): consider prophylactic artificial tears; ophthalmology referral for symptoms.

monitoring: blood glucose before each dose (hyperglycemia / DKA risk)
peripheral neuropathy assessment (sensory and motor) before each dose
skin assessment for severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN)

doseModificationRules.text: Hold enfortumab vedotin for hyperglycemia (blood glucose > 250 mg/dL) until controlled; monitor for diabetic ketoacidosis.
Hold, reduce, or discontinue for grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy per labeling; obtain clinical review.
Permanently discontinue enfortumab vedotin for grade 3-4 or suspected SJS/TEN skin reactions; urgent dermatology review.

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (BL-G): Enfortumab vedotin after PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and platinum-containing chemotherapy (references 24, 30, 31). Dosing not printed in the guideline.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for single-agent enfortumab vedotin in locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after platinum chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor (bladder #57, upper-tract #58). The dose (1.25 mg/kg IV on days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle, capped at 100 kg body weight) is sourced to DeVita 12th ed., line 20821-20827 (enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg weekly x3 of a 4-week cycle, urothelial). Enfortumab vedotin specific safety (hyperglycemia/diabetic ketoacidosis, peripheral neuropathy, severe skin reactions including SJS/TEN, ocular toxicity) is captured in supportiveCare/monitoring/doseModificationRules per the HARD RULES. Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G) establish the post-platinum/post-checkpoint setting. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
